correctness.rationale: For arbitrary one-coordinate test functions, invariance of the generator gives \(\mathbb E[x-bz\mid z]=0\), \(\mathbb E[x+ay\mid y]=0\), and \(\mathbb E[-y+z^2\mid x]=0\). The pointwise coboundary \(L(ax+y-z)=az^2+bz\) yields \(\mathbb E[z(z+b/a)]=0\). The second inspected exact identity, \(L(abz^2+ab^2x+b^2y)=a x(x+b^2/a)-a(x-bz)^2\), gives the horizontal defect. If the square defect vanishes, support invariance forces \(x=bz\), then \(y=z^2\) and \(z(b+az)=0\), so only the two equilibria remain; the converse is immediate. The zero-mean height product must take both signs for any non-equilibrium measure, giving the sharp interior/exterior height excursion, and strict positivity of the horizontal quadratic expectation forces mass outside its closed equilibrium slab. For a periodic orbit the invariant orbit measure plus continuity gives at least two boundary crossings. The checker exactly verifies both polynomial coboundaries and the canonical equilibria.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a standard chaotic-flow model into parameter-uniform, exact statistical constraints on every compact recurrent state and gives sharp excursion barriers tied to its two equilibrium coordinate levels. Conditional regressions and the defect-rigidity criterion are structural information that can constrain periodic, quasiperiodic, and chaotic invariant measures without simulation.
residual_risks: The value is qualitative/structural rather than a classification of all recurrent dynamics.

final_claim: For the generalized Sprott H flow \(\dot x=-y+z^2\), \(\dot y=x+ay\), \(\dot z=x-bz\) with \(a,b>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies the three stated one-coordinate conditional regressions, the exact height-circle identity, and the horizontal defect identity \(\mathbb E[x(x+b^2/a)]=\mathbb E[(x-bz)^2]\). Defect equality occurs exactly for measures supported on the two equilibria; every other compact invariant measure has positive mass both inside and outside the equilibrium height slab and outside the horizontal slab, and every nonconstant periodic orbit crosses the corresponding slab boundaries at least twice per least period.
limitations: Only compactly supported invariant probability measures and classical periodic orbits are covered.
The theorem does not establish existence of chaotic attractors, classify unbounded trajectories, or give a full invariant-measure classification away from the two equilibrium mixtures.
